propositions: Per-test git rev-parse HEAD calls executed ~26k times across the full suite and consume ~207 runner-seconds or 75 projected wall-seconds on macOS.
The _no_repo_commits autouse guard must detect HEAD movement, name the offending test, and preserve the allow_repo_writes escape hatch without sacrificing test-isolation fidelity.
Replacing git subprocess calls with in-process HEAD fingerprinting requires handling symbolic refs, packed refs, detached HEAD, and linked worktrees safely or falling back gracefully.

No OSS consensus exists on a fidelity-preserving implementation primitive: adding a Git library increases dependency surface; hand-parsing ref formats carries correctness risk; removing per-test attribution weakens coverage.

The optimization direction is backed by 4/4 OSS consensus (pytest, pip, Poetry, pre-commit) against per-test source-checkout Git subprocesses, but no automatically approved implementation meets both the fidelity contract and the consensus bar.
